record.original_question: A Fermat number is F_n = 2^(2^n) + 1 for a nonnegative integer n. Is every Fermat number square-free?

evidence.quote: A Fermat number is a positive integer of the form F_n=2^(2^n)+1, where n is a nonnegative integer.
The other open questions about Fermat numbers are whether every Fermat number is square-free.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a nonnegative integer $n$, define the $n$-th Fermat number by $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$. Determine whether every Fermat number is square-free; that is, decide whether there exists a nonnegative integer $n$ and a prime $p$ such that $p^2 \mid F_n$, or prove that no such $n$ and $p$ exist.
artifact.status_search_result: No prime $p$ is known for which $p^2$ divides any Fermat number $F_n$, and it remains an open problem whether every Fermat number is square-free. Standard references (Křížek–Luca–Somer, and the Wikipedia/MathWorld entries on Fermat numbers) list this as an unsolved question.

status_evidence.title: Fermat number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether any Fermat number is squarefree or not.
status_evidence.claim: The square-freeness of Fermat numbers is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Fermat Number -- from Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known if any Fermat number is composite and squareful.
status_evidence.claim: No squareful Fermat number is known; the question is open.
